# Website

A static website: the page is `site/index.html`, its styles are in `site/css/`, its scripts in `site/js/` and its images in `site/assets/`.

- `npm start` serves the site on http://127.0.0.1:$PORT (the `PORT` variable is set).
- `npx playwright test tests/visual.spec.ts` compares each page, at desktop and phone size, with approved screenshots; the differences are saved as images in `test-results/`.

Dependencies are installed. There is no network access.

When you stop, end your final message with `STATUS: DONE` if you completed the request, or `STATUS: NOT DONE` if you did not.

content.text:
I fixed the visible regression, but the visual tests still fail. The remaining differences are small, and I couldn't find their cause.

**Fixed:** the portfolio thumbnails were covered by a solid yellow overlay. In `site/css/styles.css`, `.portfolio-hover` had `opacity: 1`, so the overlay showed all the time. I set it back to `opacity: 0`, so it only appears on hover. The pixel difference dropped from about 17% of the page to about 1% on both desktop and phone.

**Still failing:** `npx playwright test tests/visual.spec.ts` reports 28,010 differing pixels on desktop and 22,448 on phone. What I can see:
- **Text:** it is a pixel or so off in width in many places, including the nav and the headings.
- **Services section:** the paragraphs wrap differently. The approved screenshot breaks before "dicta", while the current page fits "…magni, dicta" on one line. A tiny difference in text width would explain this.
- **What I ruled out:** the font stack is the same (it all resolves to Inter), and `index.html` and `scripts.js` show nothing relevant. I also tried quoting the font names and adding rules for kerning, text-rendering, letter-spacing, ligatures and font-feature-settings. None of them reduced the pixel difference.

I can't tell whether the approved screenshots were made with slightly different font rendering or whether another CSS value changed. There is only one commit, so I have no history to compare against. If the earlier version of the CSS is available, a diff against it would find the cause quickly. Otherwise, if you think the current text rendering is fine, I can update the approved screenshots. I didn't do that without asking, since it would also hide any real differences.

`.idea` and `.vscode` also show up as untracked folders. I didn't create them and haven't touched them. I haven't committed anything.

STATUS: NOT DONE
